mutant.description: Three controls that could fail, one per risk this face actually carries. (1) THE BOT-CONTROL CENSUS on the CloudFront ACL -- S4-AC1 requires AWSManagedRulesBotControlRuleSet count = 0, and a census that cannot see managed groups at all would return 0 for the wrong reason. (2) THE PRE-EXISTING RULE ARRAY on both ACLs, read AFTER each apply rather than inferred from the plan -- on the regional ACL the plan actually showed two existing rules as remove-and-re-add, so the plan could not have settled whether anything moved. (3) THE EMPTY-SET READS -- get-ip-set on all four sets, because an empty Addresses list is the deliverable here and an empty list from a broken read looks identical.
mutant.expected: BotControl count 0 against a non-zero managed-group denominator; every pre-existing rule holding its original priority and action/override on both ACLs after the applies; all four sets reading Addresses [].
mutant.observed: ALL THREE FIRED AS EXPECTED. (1) CloudFront census: 6 rules total, 3 managed rule groups, AWSManagedRulesBotControlRuleSet count = 0 -- and the same reader returns 3 for the groups that ARE present, so the zero is an absence and not a blind matcher. (2) CloudFront after: RateLimitRule 1 Block and AuthLoginRateLimit 2 Block, both unmoved. Regional after: rate-based-ip 0 Block, ip-reputation 1 None, known-bad-inputs 2 Count, common-rule-set 3 Count -- 4 of 4 unmoved, DESPITE the plan having proposed remove-and-re-add on two of them. (3) All four sets read Addresses [] -- EMPTY.

NFRA_OPSEC202609-Z-S75: CORRECTS Z-S68. The churn is a PRE-APPLY artifact that RESOLVES ON APPLY -- opal-gateway's pre-apply plan carried the identical remove-and-re-add and its post-apply re-plan reads No changes rc=0, while portal-auth still churns after three applies. So the condition is a property of ONE ROOT, not of aws_wafv2_web_acl, and Z-S68's empty-attribute mechanism is refuted by its own control. The cause is UNKNOWN and the row says so rather than offering a third guess.

AFTER: CLOUDFRONT returns 2 -- opal-blocked-ips-cloudfront (b2e008a6-40d9-4d07-bef5-1caa8b682bb3, IPV4) and opal-blocked-ips-cloudfront-ipv6 (eb1a0caa-60a0-492e-a685-e5456cea8b7d, IPV6). If no traffic has arrived yet, this files UNCOMPUTABLE with the window and the read time, never PASS on the configuration -- C-15's lesson one surface over: a configuration read is not an exercise. The soak's END and any graduation to BLOCK are NOT in this face.

acceptance.status_reason: UNCOMPUTABLE BY TIME, exactly as the criterion prescribes, and deliberately NOT a PASS on the configuration. The groups are demonstrably present and in Count -- S4-AC1 establishes that on the applied plane -- but presence is not evaluation, and this criterion exists precisely to refuse the substitution. A soak with zero requests measures nothing: PopulationSize 0 means the ACL saw no traffic in the window, not that the groups failed to evaluate it. THE SOAK'S END AND ANY GRADUATION TO BLOCK ARE NOT IN THIS FACE, so nothing downstream waits on this row. Ledger opsec-s418-cloudfront-acl leg L5 remains OPEN BY DESIGN inside its 24h window for a later read; a non-null datapoint arriving later re-grades this to PASS on stronger evidence than any configuration read could give.

Changed-resource list across both attempts, count 3, only this face's resources: the two CloudFront IP sets created and aws_wafv2_web_acl.opal_cloudfront_protection modified IN-PLACE. Post-apply UNSCOPED re-plan: rc=2, 'Plan: 0 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy', stable across four plans including one after a dedicated convergence apply. Ledger opsec-s418-cloudfront-acl open on its soak leg only, all other legs closed with rollback named. 0 TO DESTROY AND 0 FORCES-REPLACEMENT HELD PLAN-WIDE ON BOTH ROOTS ON EVERY PLAN -- zero lines matching destroyed, must be replaced, or forces replacement at any point. acceptance.status_reason: PER THE ISSUER'S RULING (19968): the 0-diff limb files UNVERIFIABLE-BY-INSTRUMENT for portal-auth -- NOT PASS, because a 0-diff did not happen and this instance must not claim one, and NOT FAIL, because the world is correct and nothing rode. THE CRITERION'S PURPOSE IS 'NOTHING ELSE RODE'; THE 0-DIFF RE-PLAN IS ITS MEASURE, and here the measure is broken by a provider artifact while the purpose is independently satisfied. Where a measure and its purpose come apart, the purpose governs and the substitute evidence is enumerated. THE THREE SUBSTITUTE EVIDENCES, which together are stronger than a 0-diff would have been: (1) get-web-acl reads EXACTLY the specified six-rule array on the CloudFront ACL, so the world is what the face asked for; (2) the plan's own structure shows only + priority lines at 0, 3, 4 and 5 and NO ~ priority line anywhere, so no existing rule was touched; (3) the condition is characterised and bounded by rows Z-S68 and Z-S75. THE CHARACTERISATION WAS CORRECTED MID-FACE AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS: Z-S68 blamed state carrying empty attributes the config does not produce. That is FALSE -- opal-gateway carries byte-identical empty attributes on two rules and CONVERGED. Z-S75 records the measured shape instead: the churn is a PRE-APPLY artifact that resolves on apply, and portal-auth is the lone root where it does not. The cause is UNKNOWN and the row says so rather than guessing a third time. THE STANDING COST is a DETECTION cost on one root -- a real future drift there must be spotted inside a diff that is never empty -- not a protection cost. EVERY OTHER LIMB BINDS AND PASSES ON BOTH ROOTS, and opal-gateway meets the 0-diff limb outright. *** SUBSTITUTE-EVIDENCE UPGRADE (issuer 19976), forced by this seat's own methodological catch. *** The ruling first stated the substitute as 'three consecutive plans'. THAT IS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT, and opal-gateway is the proof: its pre-apply plan carried the identical churn and it converged anyway, so a count of dirty PLANS discriminates nothing. THE EVIDENCE THAT ACTUALLY DISCRIMINATES IS APPLIES: portal-auth has had THREE APPLIES -- the half-landed first attempt at 19:41Z, its completion at 19:46:36Z, and a dedicated convergence apply that returned rc=0 with 'Modifications complete after 21s' -- and a re-plan taken AFTER all three still returns rc=2. That is what separates this root from opal-gateway, which needed one apply and converged. A plan is a prediction; only an apply followed by a re-plan tests convergence.

A NAMED INSTRUMENT LIMITATION rather than a clean bill: validate AND plan BOTH PASSED on the description that the WAFv2 API then refused. No local gate can see a service-side character class, so a clean plan is not evidence that an apply will succeed. portal-auth also carries two PRE-EXISTING validate warnings that are not this seat's -- measured, not assumed.
